epithet: Not sent down to distress you
lede: The Prophet ﷺ was wearing himself out, in worship and in grief over his people. This surah begins by telling him to stop — and then takes him, scene by scene, through the life of another man who was called to a task that frightened him: Mūsā, at the fire, hearing his own name.

names.name: Ṭā-Hā
names.note: The two letters it opens with. It is also called Sūrat al-Kalīm, after Mūsā, the one to whom Allah spoke.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all; Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record the agreement. Al-Qurṭubī adds that it came down before ʿUmar accepted Islam — the well-known account of his conversion has him reading its opening lines in his sister’s house — which would place it in the first five or six years. Ibn Masʿūd counted it among the earliest surahs he learned. The traditional order places it forty-fifth, directly after Maryam.
revelation.when: Makkah, in the first half of the mission — before ʿUmar’s Islam

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ طَه وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ. نَزَلَتْ قَبْلَ إِسْلَامِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

setting: Ibn al-Jawzī gives three reports of what its opening came down about, and they point the same way. One: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood so long in prayer at night that he would shift his weight from foot to foot. Another: that when the Qurʾan began to come down he and his Companions prayed at great length, and Quraysh said, “Allah has sent this Qurʾan down on Muḥammad only to make him miserable.” The surah answers: “Ṭā-Hā. We have not sent down the Qurʾan to you that you should be distressed, but as a reminder for whoever fears.”

It is the surah connected with the turning of ʿUmar. The account, which Ibn Isḥāq relates and which al-Qurṭubī cites here, is that he set out with his sword to kill the Prophet ﷺ, was told on the way that his own sister and her husband had become Muslims, burst in on them, struck her — and then, shamed by the sight of her blood, asked to see what they had been reading. It was a sheet with the opening of this surah. The chains of the story are not strong, and it is told as a report.

What fills most of the surah is Mūsā, and here the telling stays close to him as a person. He sees a fire and tells his family to wait. He hears: “I am your Lord, so take off your sandals… I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.” He is asked what is in his hand, and answers at length, like a man glad to be spoken to. He is told to go to Pharaoh, and asks for his chest to be opened, his task made easy, the knot loosed from his tongue, and his brother given to him as a helper. When he and Hārūn say they are afraid, they are told: “Do not fear. I am with you both; I hear and I see.”

The Prophet ﷺ is being shown that the fear is not new, and neither is the answer. The surah ends as it began, speaking to him directly: be patient with what they say; glorify your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; do not stretch your eyes towards what We have given some of them to enjoy; and bid your family to pray, and be steadfast in it.

occasions.title: “Only to make him miserable”
occasions.text: When the Qurʾan came down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he and his Companions prayed and stood for long. Quraysh said: “Allah has sent down this Qurʾan upon Muḥammad only so that he should be wretched.” So this was revealed.
occasions.source: Ibn al-Jawzī, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk — one of three accounts he gives.

evidence.quote: أنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ لَمّا نَزَلَ عَلَيْهِ القُرْآنُ صَلّى هو وأصْحابُهُ فَأطالَ القِيامَ، فَقالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ: ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذا القُرْآنَ عَلى مُحَمَّدٍ إلّا لِيَشْقى، فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ

aim: To strengthen the Prophet ﷺ to bear the message, and to be patient upon it.
themes: The Qurʾan as a reminder, not a burden

outline.title: Not to distress you
outline.summary: Ṭā-Hā. We have not sent down the Qurʾan to you that you should be distressed, but only as a reminder for whoever fears: a sending down from Him who created the earth and the high heavens — the Most Merciful, who rose over the Throne. Allah: there is no god but He. His are the most beautiful names.

outline.title: The fire, and the commission
outline.summary: Has the story of Mūsā reached you? He saw a fire. When he came to it, he was called: “Mūsā, I am your Lord; take off your sandals — you are in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā. I am Allah; there is no god but I, so worship Me, and establish the prayer for My remembrance.” The staff, and the hand. “Go to Pharaoh; he has transgressed.” — “My Lord, open my chest for me, ease my task, loose the knot from my tongue, and give me a helper from my family: Hārūn, my brother.” — “You are granted your request, Mūsā.”

outline.title: “I made you for Myself”
outline.summary: We had already shown you favour another time: when We inspired your mother to cast you into the river; when your sister walked along; when you killed a man and We saved you from distress; then you came here as ordained. “I have made you for Myself. Go, you and your brother… Speak to him gently; perhaps he will take heed, or fear.” — “Our Lord, we fear he will be hasty against us.” — “Do not fear; I am with you both, hearing and seeing.” — “Who is your Lord, Mūsā?” — “Our Lord is He who gave everything its form, then guided.”

outline.title: The day of the festival
outline.summary: Pharaoh denied and refused, and set a contest for the day of the festival. The sorcerers cast their ropes and staffs, and Mūsā felt fear within himself. “Do not fear; you will be uppermost. Throw what is in your right hand.” The sorcerers fell in prostration: “We believe in the Lord of Hārūn and Mūsā.” Pharaoh threatened them with crucifixion: “Decree, then, whatever you will decree; you decree only for this life.” Mūsā was told to lead My servants out by night, and Pharaoh followed with his hosts, and the sea covered them.

outline.title: The calf
outline.summary: Children of Israel, We saved you from your enemy. — “What made you hurry ahead of your people, Mūsā?” We tried your people after you, and the Sāmirī led them astray: he brought out for them a calf, a body that lowed. Hārūn had told them, “My people, you are only being tested by it.” Mūsā returned in anger and grief; he seized his brother by the head. “And you, Sāmirī?” — “I saw what they did not see.” Your god is only Allah.

outline.title: The Day, and the Qurʾan
outline.summary: Thus We relate to you the news of what has gone before, and We have given you a reminder from Ourselves. They ask you about the mountains: say, my Lord will scatter them as dust. That Day they will follow the caller, without deviation, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful. Do not hasten with the Qurʾan before its revelation to you is completed, and say: “My Lord, increase me in knowledge” (20:114).

outline.title: Ādam forgot
outline.summary: We made a covenant with Ādam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve. Satan whispered to him: “Shall I show you the tree of eternity?” They ate; then his Lord chose him, turned to him and guided him. “Whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor be wretched. But whoever turns away from My Reminder will have a straitened life, and We shall raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection.”

outline.title: Be patient, and pray
outline.summary: So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and in the hours of the night, and at the ends of the day. Do not stretch your eyes towards what We have given some of them to enjoy. Bid your family to pray, and be steadfast in it; We ask no provision of you — We provide for you. Say: everyone is waiting; so wait.

keyAyah.why: The first thing Mūsā was told after his name: who is speaking, and what follows from it — worship, and the prayer.

virtues.text: “Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers; there is no expiation for it but that. ‘Establish the prayer for My remembrance.’”
virtues.arabic: مَنْ نَسِيَ صَلاَةً فَلْيُصَلِّ إِذَا ذَكَرَهَا

virtues.text: Ibn Masʿūd counted it, with Banī Isrāʾīl, al-Kahf, Maryam and al-Anbiyāʾ, among “the first and finest” — the earliest surahs he had learned.

virtuesNote: Ibn Kathīr opens his commentary with a report that Allah recited Ṭā-Hā and Yā-Sīn a thousand years before creating Ādam, and says of it at once that it is a strange report with something objectionable in it, two of its narrators having been criticised.
before: Maryam ended by saying that the Qurʾan was made easy on his tongue to bring good news and warning. Ṭā-Hā opens: it was not sent to make you wretched.
after: Ṭā-Hā ends: everyone is waiting, so wait. Al-Anbiyāʾ begins: their reckoning has drawn near to mankind, while they turn away, heedless.

notable.label: The Most Merciful rose over the Throne
“I am Allah… establish the prayer for My remembrance”
Mūsā’s prayer: “open my chest for me”
“I am with you both; I hear and I see”
